craft_notes: Sthāyin: adbhuta of world mirrored whole; vyabhicāri wonder at bearing-by-mirroring. Sanskrit-first: viśvabharita (WORLD-BEARING — mark first, per argmap character-then-mechanism); svadṛk (OWN-SEEING — kept technical); śakti-darpaṇa (power-mirror — manner IS the mark). Rows: 10 (mirror left standing, no gloss), 1 (‘mirrored by power’ closes — karaṇa last), 7 (Bhairava named L1 — mark before manner). Close: ‘mirrored by power’. Rupture: semicolon (mark turns to mechanism). Rejected: ‘in the mirror of His vision’ — killed: smoothing loses svadṛk; ‘carries’ — killed: bearing is BY-mirroring; ‘the universe’ — killed: ‘the whole’ kept (kṛtsna totality). Read aloud: HE a-LONE is BHAI-ra-va, the WORLD-bear-ing GOD … IN-his-OWN-see-ing's MIR-ror STANDS the WHOLE, MIR-rored BY-pow-ER.

lines: He alone is Bhairava, the world-bearing god;
in His own seeing's mirror stands the whole, mirrored by power.
l4.sanskrit_cite: sa eva bhairavo devo jagadbharaṇalakṣaṇaḥ | svātmādṛṣe samagraṃ hi yacchaktyā pratibimbitam

reads_against.argmap: How does Bhairava bear the world? → Character then mechanism: world-bearing mark, power-mirroring manner.
c1_essence: World-bearing His mark; whole mirrored by power in self-seeing.
